title: Keep task-data Git operations running for at least sixty seconds
outcome: New task-data worktree Git operations use at least a sixty-second abort limit and log one non-interrupting warning after ten seconds, preserving the caller's absolute deadline and atomic recovery behavior.
acceptance: The new task-data worktree and commit query paths use an abort allowance of at least sixty seconds, admitted by the shared Git query layer; an existing longer allowance is preserved, and internal remaining time stays tied to the same absolute operation deadline.

An operation still running after ten seconds emits one bounded warning with operation or attempt identity and elapsed time, without interrupting it or exposing a complete source_id; behavioral coverage proves the warning and abort boundaries and unchanged refusal or retry atomicity.

completion.summary: Implemented at-least-sixty-second task-data and exchange request deadlines with one bounded ten-second warning, preserving longer allowances, spent absolute deadlines and recovery semantics.
